RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of bias; panel compositions typically reflect available leadership or administrative staff. While your formal leadership credentials appear stronger on paper, principal appointments heavily weigh interview performance, strategic vision, references, and institutional fit, where substantial teaching experience is also valued.

Accusing the panel of bias based solely on their gender is speculative and will damage your professional reputation. While unconscious bias is always possible in subjective evaluations, you currently lack supporting evidence. 

Instead of raising the panel's demographics, send a polite follow-up requesting your written explanation. Focus entirely on the objective scoring rubrics and feedback to understand the decision.
